acceptedAnswer.text: The office areas of industrial sites — plant offices, warehouse offices and facility administration areas — with their workstations and desks, office furniture, files and records runs, fixtures and office equipment, including the packing, protection and placement that goes with them (1). The job runs the full chain: survey, phased plan, pack and label, sequenced move, install and place, verify, close-out (1).

mainEntity.name: What does an industrial office move include?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no universal order — the sequence is set at the survey by one question: what can the site afford to have dark, and for how long? The published approach phases the move by zone or department, keeps the functions the operation depends on running longest, and decides what leaves first and what arrives first before move day — never on the day (1).

mainEntity.name: Office or warehouse first, when both are moving?

acceptedAnswer.text: Honestly: no downtime figure and no restart guarantee is published for this service, and we will not quote you one (1). What the model actually does is structural — a phased plan built around production and site access, non-critical sections moved while others keep operating, landing spots decided before move day, and a verify-and-close-out step so the site is working again on day one (1).

Commonly, yes: industrial sites and commercial buildings commonly ask movers for a certificate naming the building or site, with limits and any additional-insured wording set by the site, not the mover (1). A certificate is a one-page proof of coverage, not the policy itself (3). Ours is confirmed per job at quote time — send the site's exact wording with your quote request (1).

mainEntity.name: Will the site ask for a certificate of insurance?

acceptedAnswer.text: They split out at the survey. Servers, racks and network equipment are handled under the separate IT Relocation category when they fall in its scope (1). Any single item of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs — a safe or fire file in the office area — moves under SIR Structural Integrity Relocation and the KIM-GS Protocol, with the floor check referencing L/360, before anything is lifted (1).

mainEntity.name: How are servers, racks and heavy items handled?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every job is reviewed in full — scope, distance, manpower and equipment — and priced at one flat rate, never hourly, agreed in writing before move day under our standing promise, Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free! (1) The drivers are the ones you control: workstation and file-run counts, phasing, move windows, access at both ends, distance, packing scope, staging, and any high-mass item surveyed into the same rate (1).
